title: Lazarus session
description:
A session descriptor and its lifecycle. A session is temporary and is never published: it has no ingress route, no subdomain, and no long-lived publicly reachable address (ADR-0012).

This contract deliberately carries no command text and no output. User history lives in the client, and the server stores only what it needs to route a reconnection and reap an expiry (ADR-0019). A transcript is the most sensitive data Lazarus holds, and nothing in the product queries it server-side.

ticket.description: Present on start and on reissue. Absent once a ticket has been redeemed, so a reconnected client cannot retain a usable credential.

hubUrl.description: Where to subscribe for events. Always a root-relative path resolved against the operator-configured base address, never an absolute host and never protocol-relative, so no code path can hardcode or be redirected to an endpoint (AGENTS.md section 5).

sessionState.description: The session lifecycle position. Exhaustive by construction: the generated type is a union of literals, so a client switch on it is checked at compile time. Per-state payloads live on the event that carries the transition, not as nullable fields on the descriptor.

sessionDescriptor.description: Everything the server stores about a session. If a field is not here, the server does not have it.

tenantId.description: Derived from the validated token at session start. Never from a request body, query parameter, or URL segment, so a caller can never choose their tenant.

expiresAt.description: Server-enforced expiry. The client does not decide when a session ends, and expiry is reaped by the platform rather than by whoever is still connected.

environmentImage.description: The digest-pinned image this session resolved to. Recorded for audit and reproducibility; a tag is not an identity.

failureCode.description: Present when state is 'failed'. A stable code, never an internal exception message.

sessionLimits.description: The bounds a session was admitted under. Returned so a client can explain a refusal before it happens rather than after.

reconnectionTicket.description: A short-lived, single-use ticket that lets a client rejoin its own session. Deliberately not the session id: a guessable identifier that reattached on its own would be an authentication bypass.

sessionEvent.description: A lifecycle transition delivered to subscribers. Execution output is a separate stream: this one carries state changes and lets a client stop listening.
